title: Herschel Evans and Lester Young: rivalry and respect
summary: The two tenors would not speak or face each other on stage, but respected one another.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well how about the relationship between, I mean Basie always had two contrasting tenors. Now were they usually good friends or was there ever ......

Herschel and Lester on the outside you wouldn't think that they liked each other. I remember one time, Herschel got mad at me because he said I was making arrangements with all the solo for Lester. And I said, well look, I said, don't be made at me. I said, Basie asked me to make it like that.

Now he wanted Lester to play all the fast songs and Hershel to play the slow ones, you see. "Blue and Sentimental." But Herschel always wanted to play something else besides that too. So Herschel wouldn't speak to me for about a month. Because he thought that I was making arrangements and putting him, giving the solos to Lester. And he and Lester wasn't speaking to each other. In fact when they sat on the band stand they were on the opposite ends, they still would turn their chairs away from the other two guys in the middle.
Herschel would turn his back and Lester would turn his back. So you got five saxophones, three of

them playing forward and two playing out on the sides. Because they didn't even want to face each other. But they did respect each other as being good tenor players. Although they played different styles.
Herschel couldn't play like Lester and Lester couldn't play like Herschel. But they never, didn't have anything to do with each other. But except that they did respect each other.
Well they, what about the later ones. You know when they had Byas and Lucky Thompson, Buddy Tate and.....
They were not, there were no sort of jealousy or.....
